meaning: Numbers for the fingers: thumb 1, pointing finger 2, middle 3, ring 4, little finger 5, the same on both hands.
whyItMatters: Music and teachers use them to say which finger plays each note.

meaning: How the hand sits on the keys: fingers curved, fingertips on the keys, wrist level and loose.
whyItMatters: Curved fingers are stronger and quicker, and a loose hand does not tire or hurt.

meaning: Each finger resting over its own key on five white keys side by side, such as C to G.
whyItMatters: Many first tunes fit in one position, so you can play them without moving or looking.

meaning: Moving one finger while the others stay still and relaxed.
whyItMatters: It makes melodies even and keeps notes from smearing together.

meaning: The plan for which finger plays each key, often printed as small numbers over the notes.
whyItMatters: A good plan never leaves you without a finger for the next key.

meaning: Going up with the right hand (or down with the left), the thumb slides under the fingers to the next key and the hand follows.
whyItMatters: It carries a scale past five keys without a gap.

meaning: Coming down with the right hand (or up with the left), finger 3 reaches over the thumb to the next key.
whyItMatters: It brings a run back the other way as smoothly as thumb under took it out.

meaning: Thumb and little finger stretched an octave apart, so both keys with the same name play together.
whyItMatters: Keeping the shape and moving the whole hand makes octaves land without looking.

meaning: Lifting the whole hand and landing it in a new place, already shaped for what it plays next.
whyItMatters: Shaping the hand in the air is what makes jumping chords land cleanly.

meaning: A chord whose notes are played one after another instead of all at once.
whyItMatters: Left-hand parts are full of them; a still hand and busy fingers make them fast and even.

meaning: A move from one key to another far away, more than a hand-width.
whyItMatters: Leaps are aimed with the eyes first; looking at the landing key before moving makes them reliable.
